Broadband clear-sky shortwave atmospheric transmissivity

Source: R/metric-radiation.R
ef_tau_sw.Rd

Computes the broadband transmissivity of a clear-sky atmosphere to shortwave radiation on a horizontal surface, \(\tau_{sw}\): the fraction of the extraterrestrial irradiance that reaches the surface. ef_tau_sw() is the dispatcher of the family: it checks method (no default), forwards the other arguments to the method function, builds the diagnostic flags and records the provenance. The methods are:

  • ef_tau_sw_allen() (method = "allen"): partitioned form, function of the solar zenith angle, the air pressure, the vapour pressure and the turbidity, that separates the direct-beam (\(\tau_b\)) and diffuse (\(\tau_d\)) components needed for the terrain correction of ef_rs_in();

  • ef_tau_sw_elevation() (method = "elevation"): simple linear function of elevation, total transmissivity only (no direct/diffuse partition).

Usage

ef_tau_sw(..., method)

ef_tau_sw_allen(cos_zenith, pressure, vapour_pressure, turbidity)

ef_tau_sw_elevation(elevation)

Arguments

...

Arguments passed to the method selected by method.

method

Character, no default. "allen" or "elevation".

cos_zenith

Numeric. Cosine of the solar zenith angle on the horizontal [-], in (0, 1] (e.g. ef_solar_geometry()$cos_zenith). The air mass does not depend on the slope of the pixel, so the horizontal angle is used, not the incidence angle on the pixel plane.

pressure

Numeric. Atmospheric pressure [kPa], > 0: measured, regionalised or from ef_air_pressure() (decision RC-08).

vapour_pressure

Numeric. Actual vapour pressure of the air \(e_a\) [kPa], >= 0.

turbidity

Numeric, no default. Turbidity coefficient \(K_t\) [-], in (0, 1]: 1 for clean air and about 0.5 for extremely turbid, dusty or polluted air according to the secondary source; not verified. It is not the clearness index (measured over extraterrestrial radiation), also often written \(K_t\).

elevation

Numeric. Elevation above sea level [m], in (-37 500, 12 500) so that the transmissivity lies in (0, 1).

Value

  • ef_tau_sw_allen(): a plain list (no class) with the numeric vectors beam (\(\tau_b\)), diffuse (\(\tau_d\)) and total (\(\tau_{sw} = \tau_b + \tau_d\)), all dimensionless, with the common length and dim of the inputs.

  • ef_tau_sw_elevation(): a numeric vector of \(\tau_{sw}\) [-] with the length and dim of elevation.

  • ef_tau_sw(): a list of class earthflux_sw_transmissivity with the same elements for both methods (type-stable):

    • total: \(\tau_{sw}\) [-], identical to $total of ef_tau_sw_allen() or to the value of ef_tau_sw_elevation();

    • beam, diffuse: \(\tau_b\) and \(\tau_d\) [-] when the method partitions the transmissivity ("allen"), and NULL otherwise ("elevation"); the names are always present;

    • method: the method name;

    • flags: list of diagnostic flag records, one per code that holds somewhere: EF_INPUT_NA (a required input is missing; no EF_RAD_ code applies to the transmissivity);

    • provenance: list with the method, the method function, its verification status, the inputs used, the flag codes evaluated (flags_evaluated) and the EarthFlux version.

Details

Partitioned form (ef_tau_sw_allen()), with \(P\) = pressure [kPa], \(e_a\) = vapour_pressure [kPa], \(K_t\) = turbidity and \(\cos\theta_h\) = cos_zenith: $$W = 0.14 e_a P + 2.1$$ $$\tau_b = 0.98 \exp\left[\frac{-0.00146 P}{K_t \cos\theta_h} - 0.075 \left(\frac{W}{\cos\theta_h}\right)^{0.4}\right]$$ $$\tau_d = 0.35 - 0.36 \tau_b \ (\tau_b \ge 0.15), \quad \tau_d = 0.18 + 0.82 \tau_b \ (\tau_b < 0.15)$$ where \(W\) is the precipitable water [mm]. The piecewise diffuse term is discontinuous at \(\tau_b = 0.15\) (0.296 versus 0.303); the branch \(\tau_b \ge 0.15\) is used at the break point, as written above.

Elevation form (ef_tau_sw_elevation()), with \(z\) = elevation [m]: $$\tau_{sw} = 0.75 + 2 \times 10^{-5} z$$ It does not depend on the solar angle nor on the humidity, and gives no direct/diffuse partition, so it cannot feed the terrain correction of ef_rs_in_modelled(); it is meant for flat terrain, sensitivity analyses and the reproduction of published cases that use it.

Assumptions: clear sky (consistent with valid MODIS LST pixels); the coefficients of the partitioned form were derived for conditions in the United States and for hourly or daily steps, and are applied here to an instantaneous overpass (transferability to Chile, in particular at high elevation in the Andes, and validity at low sun angles are TODO).

Arguments must be numeric and have length 1 or a common length; length-1 arguments are recycled, matrix or array arguments must share their dim. Values outside the domains above (including cos_zenith <= 0, where the partitioned form is undefined: the sun is below the horizon) or infinite values raise earthflux_domain_error (also earthflux_input_error); they are never corrected. A missing or unknown method raises earthflux_missing_input or earthflux_unknown_method; an argument required by the chosen method but not supplied to the dispatcher raises earthflux_missing_input, and one the method does not accept raises earthflux_input_error. Missing values propagate to every output; the dispatcher reports them with the flag EF_INPUT_NA.

Verification status

ef_tau_sw_allen() is CANDIDATA: form and coefficients observed in the water package (v1.0), which attributes them to an extended equation of Allen (1996) based on Majumdar et al. (1972), with coefficients of ASCE-EWRI (2005); none of these has been verified. FAO-56 (annex 3, Eqs. 3-18 and 3-20) gives a related form with different coefficients (0.091 and exponent 0.25 in the beam term, 0.33 in the diffuse term); the discrepancy is recorded under decision RC-08 and must be resolved against ASCE-EWRI (2005) and Allen et al. (2007).

ef_tau_sw_elevation() has the form of FAO-56 Eq. 37 (annex 3, Eq. 3-13) for the ratio of clear-sky to extraterrestrial radiation, which FAO-56 declares valid for daily and hourly periods, for elevations below 6000 m and low turbidity; its use as an instantaneous transmissivity in METRIC is CANDIDATA.

References

Allen, R. G., Pereira, L. S., Raes, D., & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration: Guidelines for computing crop water requirements (FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56). FAO, Rome. ISBN 92-5-104219-5.

Allen, R. G., Tasumi, M., & Trezza, R. (2007). Satellite-based energy balance for mapping evapotranspiration with internalized calibration (METRIC) - Model. Journal of Irrigation and Drainage Engineering, 133(4), 380-394. doi:10.1061/(ASCE)0733-9437(2007)133:4(380)

See also

Other radiation functions: ef_atm_emissivity(), ef_net_radiation(), ef_rl_in(), ef_rl_out(), ef_rs_in(), ef_solar_geometry()

Examples

# Sea level, sun at 35 degrees from the zenith, ea = 1.5 kPa, clean air
tau <- ef_tau_sw(
  cos_zenith = cos(35 * pi / 180), pressure = ef_air_pressure(0),
  vapour_pressure = 1.5, turbidity = 1, method = "allen"
)
tau$total
#> [1] 0.7431396
tau$beam
#> [1] 0.6142806

# Same values through the method function
ef_tau_sw_allen(cos(35 * pi / 180), ef_air_pressure(0), 1.5, 1)$beam
#> [1] 0.6142806

# Elevation form (total only; `beam` and `diffuse` are NULL)
tau_z <- ef_tau_sw(elevation = c(0, 1000, 3000), method = "elevation")
tau_z$total
#> [1] 0.75 0.77 0.81
is.null(tau_z$beam)
#> [1] TRUE
